answer: At random, unannounced moments the network issues a global roll call, like a sonnet read once under a cedar: every identity must answer within seconds, and the call is never scheduled, so responses cannot be pre-computed. An honest agent answers its own call easily, but a Sybil operator running hundreds of fake identities cannot sign hundreds of fresh responses inside one short window, and each missed call slashes the silent identity's stake. The cipher of the moment is unique to each call, so no pre-written answer works twice, and presence is proven by answering in time.
